one_month_reasoning: No scheduled company catalyst falls between 2026-09-30 and 2026-10-29: Q1 FY27 results are normally reported in the third week of November, after the window, and the fiscal-2027 guide ($23.3-23.5B revenue, non-GAAP EPS $22.88-23.12) came out on Aug 25. The October 15 tax-extension deadline is immaterial to reported numbers. Possible unscheduled moves: news in the securities class action (lead-plaintiff deadline was Sept 8), more AI tax or bookkeeping agent launches (Perplexity, OpenAI, Anthropic/Xero), and broker target cuts. The stock is near its 52-week low after falling from $315 to $268 since the guide. Mean-reversion and continued negative momentum roughly cancel out, so I use a nearly symmetric lognormal centred at about $268 with a 1-month sigma of 13%, a bit below 50%/3.5 because there is no event in the window. The median is tilted 1 point above today because of the $5B+/yr buyback.

fair_value.method: Blend of 13x FY28 (NTM at horizon) EPS including SBC (~$25.5 -> $332) and an 8% FCF-after-SBC yield on ~$25.5/share (-> $319); weights 50/50, giving about $322 by Sept 2027.

inputs_detail.input: FY27 non-GAAP EPS guidance (now includes SBC)

inputs_detail.value: $23.94 (24 down vs 5 up revisions in 30 days)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 guide $23.00 grown about 11%. Revenue growth slows to about 8%, with GBS at 12-13% and Consumer at 2-4% as TurboTax keeps giving up ARPC to AI-native and low-cost rivals (Goldman's FY28 is 13% below consensus). Margin gains from the 17% headcount cut and about 2% share count reduction. H&R Block gaining assisted share and IRS data showing DIY e-file up only ~1.7% both limit unit growth.

The stock trades at about 11.6x FY27 guidance and the forward P/E was about 13x at $292 (24/7). I hold the multiple near today's disrupted-regime level instead of the historical 30x+, because Goldman's AI cost-per-return argument ($0.12 vs $162 ARPC) and JPM/BofA downgrades mean a structural re-rating is unlikely within 12 months. I give a small premium over today for 9-10% revenue growth and the GBS mix.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY27E FCF after SBC ~$6.9B / ~270M shares = $25.5/share at 8% yield

inputs_detail.value: 277M FY26 average, ~270M in FY27 after $5.5B/yr buybacks
inputs_detail.derivation: 277M reduced by about 2.5% at the FY26 buyback pace
OCF grows about 8% to $9.5B, minus about $0.35B capex, minus about $1.6B SBC, is about $7.5B; I haircut that to $6.9B for price investment in TurboTax, then divide by 270M shares.

This is a high-uncertainty, possibly ex-growth consumer franchise with 2-3% TurboTax unit growth, so 8% sits between mature-software yields of 4-5% and ex-growth value yields of 10%. It is consistent with Morningstar moving to High uncertainty.

bear.story: The 2027 tax season (Jan-Apr) shows TurboTax units falling as Perplexity, ChatGPT/Claude-based agents and low-cost rivals scale in their second season. Intuit cuts ARPC further, and AI bookkeeping agents at Xero and others slow QuickBooks. FY28 EPS comes in around $21 and the multiple falls to about 8.5x on terminal-decline fears.

base.story: TurboTax revenue is flat to +3% as price cuts partly retain units. GBS grows 12-13% and Credit Karma is solid. Buybacks of about $5B/yr support EPS, FY28 EPS is about $25, and the multiple stays near 12x.

bull.story: The 2027 tax season shows the lower price stopped DIY share loss (IRS self-prep counts up, AI rivals mostly stuck at drafting rather than e-filing). QBO Advanced and Intuit Assist monetize. FY28 EPS reaches about $26.5 and the multiple re-rates to about 16x, close to Mizuho's $430 target.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $200 the stock trades under 8.7x FY27 guided EPS and under a 12% FCF-after-SBC yield. That would most likely mean FY27 guidance is being cut, for example at the Q2 report in Feb 2027 or on tax-season data showing TurboTax units shrinking, or that QuickBooks net adds are turning down under AI-agent competition. Either would point to structural share loss rather than a de-rating on sentiment.

Start of IRS 2027 filing season; weekly IRS self-prepared e-file statistics and launches from AI tax rivals
Q2 FY27 results and early-season TurboTax unit commentary
Tax day; IRS end-of-season self-prep counts and H&R Block DIY/assisted data
Q3 FY27 results with TurboTax season scorecard (the key print)
Q4 FY27 results and FY28 guidance
Securities class action progress; state or FTC probes into TurboTax practices
AI-agent product launches in tax and bookkeeping (Perplexity, OpenAI, Xero/Anthropic)

key_uncertainties: Whether AI agents move from drafting returns to actually e-filing and taking DIY share at scale in the 2027 season
How far TurboTax ARPC falls to defend units, since management accepts lower initial DIY ARPC
Whether AI-agent disruption spreads to QuickBooks, which is 60% of revenue and the main growth engine
Whether the market multiple stabilizes near 12x or keeps compressing like other AI-disrupted software names
Litigation and regulatory exposure around TurboTax marketing and pricing
reasoning: Industry-chain evidence is mixed rather than catastrophic. IRS data shows self-prepared e-file returns up about 1.7-1.9% in the 2026 season, so the DIY category is not shrinking. Direct File has been cancelled with no return date, which removes a government-competition overhang. H&R Block (FY26 revenue +5%) gained assisted share for a third year and grew Wave, and Intuit's own figures show TurboTax revenue +7% with guided units +2-3% and share lost at the price-sensitive end. The new competitors are real and cheap: Perplexity's tax agent comes with a $17/mo Pro plan (it drafts returns rather than filing them), Goldman estimates AI costs about $0.12 per return against TurboTax's roughly $162 ARPC, and Xero is shipping AI features with Anthropic. That argues for ongoing price compression rather than a collapse within 12 months. The market already prices a lot in: $268 is about 11.6x FY27 EPS guidance that now includes SBC, with roughly an 11% FCF yield before SBC and $5.5B/yr of buybacks. My fair value of about $322 uses 13x FY28 EPS of about $25.5 and an 8% FCF-after-SBC yield. Scenarios are bear $175 (25%), base $300 (50%) and bull $430 (25%), for a mean of about $301. For the ladder I use a lognormal with median about $290 and sigma 0.40, slightly fatter on the left, which is below the trailing 50% realized volatility (inflated by the de-rating) but above a normal large-cap's 25-35%. The result is P(>=268) about 0.58. Research was limited to about 12 queries.
